haiku-low.q1: Before ready. Keys load at startup; /healthz returns 200 only after all three keys are loaded, so a pod is not ready until then.
haiku-low.q2: One attempt, 3 retries 2 seconds apart (about 6 seconds), then non-zero exit. Kubernetes restarts it; the rollout halts while old pods keep serving.
haiku-low.q3: A 5-minute refresh swaps in any changed version. A failed read keeps the last good value, logs a warning and retries at the next run.
haiku-low.q4: In process memory only, in the secret holder. Never on disk, in environment variables, or in logs; logs show only secret names and version ids.
haiku-low.q5: Production pods under orders-api-prod have read-only access to orders-api/prod/*. Only the security on-call role can write prod secrets.
haiku-low.q6: Git history keeps the old values, and old images contain them. Rotating each key at its provider makes the old value useless.
haiku-low.q7: The client calls the secret holder for the current key on every provider call. It does not copy the key when the client is built.
haiku-low.q8: Each pod's logs show all three written version ids after the last replacement, covering a refresh cycle; all 4 pods run the new image digest.
haiku-low.q9: Overlap, store access, new provider keys, store writes, code switch with config keys removed, then revoking old keys.
haiku-low.q10: Non-secret config/app.yaml plus orders-api/dev/* read with the developer's dev-only identity; dev or sandbox keys only, never live keys.
haiku-low.q11: It is treated the same as an unreachable store: the pod never becomes ready and exits non-zero after the same retries. The plan flags this for confirmation.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first (all three read from the store into memory at startup); the pod reports ready (/healthz 200) only after all three are loaded.
sonnet.q2: It retries (one attempt plus 3 retries, 2s apart, ~6s), logs the failure without secrets, and exits non-zero; Kubernetes restarts it with backoff. The rollout halts, and old pods keep serving on their current keys, so live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A background refresh every 5 minutes (with random jitter) re-reads all three secrets; if a version id changed, it atomically swaps the new value into the secret holder, no restart. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning (secret name and error class), and retries at the next run; requests are unaffected.
sonnet.q4: Held in process memory only, in the secret holder (redacted text form). Must never appear on disk, in environment variables, or in logs (also not in tickets, chat, the repo, or error messages/request headers).
sonnet.q5: Read of prod: the service identity orders-api-prod (read-only on orders-api/prod/*). Write: only the security on-call role. Engineers can read only dev secrets, not prod.
sonnet.q6: The keys remain in git history (two years) and are treated as leaked; history is not rewritten. Rotating each key at its provider and revoking the old ones makes the old values useless.
sonnet.q7: The provider client asks the secret holder for the current key on every call; it does not copy the key when built, so refreshed values take effect.
sonnet.q8: Confirmation step: all 4 pods run the new image digest, and each pod's logs show the recorded version ids for all three keys (at startup or refresh), with a log window covering at least one full refresh cycle after the last pod was replaced; if a newer version id exists, check against it. If any check fails, don't revoke. Security on-call then approves.
sonnet.q9: 1) Confirm provider overlap; 2) set up store entries and access rules; 3) issue new keys at the providers (rotating, old still active); 4) write new keys to the store; 5) ship code reading from the store and removing keys from the config file (staging then prod rollout); 6) confirm; 7) revoke old keys; 8) clean up.
sonnet.q10: From the secret store's orders-api/dev/* secrets (provider sandbox or agreed test keys, never live), read into memory using the developer's own dev-only identity. Fallback: opt-in sandbox or local stub via base_url.
sonnet.q11: It is treated like an unreachable store: the pod never becomes ready, retries (one attempt plus 3 retries, 2s apart), then exits non-zero. The plan flags this as needing confirmation.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Rotation cadence is undecided; the plan sets none, and the 5-minute refresh is not a rotation policy.
